title: Appetizers
description:
This recipe is from the “Guacamole Napkin” that Liz brought over for Easter 2009 – so simple and so tasty.
If you have avocados that are not quite ripe, you can put them into a paper bag for a day or so with another piece of fruit, such as a banana. Magically (actually, scientifically), it works!
Appetizers – Three Quick and Easy Ones
With a very sharp knife, finely dice the salmon.
Whisk the crème fraiche for a minute or so, then fold in all the chopped ingredients. Season with salt and white pepper to taste.
Fill the phyllo cups with a tablespoon or so of the salmon mixture.
Garnish with a little chive cutting or a piece of parsley and serve.
ingredients: 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese, or mixture with Locatelli
2 tablespoons onions or shallots, finely chopped
1 baguette, sliced on bias for little toasts
1 teaspoon shallots, finely chopped chives or parsley, for garnish
directions: This is based on the “Cornets” recipe from “The French Laundry Cookbook” and is a whole lot easier to make than the actual cornets (though you may want to try that some time). Feel free to substitute a sour cream and cream cheese or mascarpone mixture for the crème fraiche. And, you can mix up the onion flavors as well.
Mix the cheese, mayonnaise, and onions together.
Spoon the cheese mixture in a rounded heap onto the baguette slices.
Bake for 8-10 minutes, until the cheese is browned and bubbly.
Serve immediately (but don’t burn your tongue!).

Some people at some points in their lives – young Gall girls, for example – don’t like the onions in the mixture, so you can leave it out if you want. But these are much tastier with this little extra spice.
Peel and coarsely mash the avocado in a bowl.
Stir in the remaining ingredients and season generously with salt and a little pepper.
Chill and serve with chips (maybe a Margarita!).
